messages:
alex: Heads up — trying to scale a 64-GPU job in us-west1 and the k8s nodes keep failing to join because of pod IP exhaustion. Can someone check our VPC secondary range and ENI quotas?

maya: Oof. Is this on AWS or GCP cluster? Which CNI?

alex: AWS (eks-prod-gpu-usw1). Using aws-vpc-cni v1.12. Events show `InsufficientIPs` on new nodes.

ben: That error usually means the node ENI/IP quota for the instance type is hit. Which instance family? p4d or g5?

alex: g5. We're using mixed nodepools: g5.2x, g5.8x. For g5.8x we expected ~60 pods/node but kubelet max-pods is down to 30 because of IP limits.

judy: I see similar in cluster-autoscaler logs from last scale attempt: `failed to launch instance: quotaExceeded: The maximum number of ENIs has been reached in zone us-west-1a` (snippet copied).

alex: Copy of kubelet output:
```
W0413 14:12:02.345 kubelet_node_status.go:500] Failed to allocate pod IP: InsufficientIPs: instance i-0abc... cannot attach more IPs
```

maya: Two things: request increase for ENI & IPv4 addresses in the account (per AZ) and consider enabling the AWS CNI plugin pod ENI support (warm IP target) or switch to prefix delegation (secondary private IPs per ENI) for higher density. Also we can lower max-pods per node via kubelet but that doesn't solve the IP scarcity.

ben: Agreed. Also check account's elastic network interfaces quota and EC2 local addresses. I can open a support case to AWS for `Network Interfaces per Region` and `IPv4 addresses per ENI` increase.

alex: Can we include a request for per-subnet auto-assign/secondary CIDR increase? We're currently at /20s for the gpu-subnet and that runs out fast when nodepools scale. Region-wide GPU capacity is OK but networking is the choke.

judy: Cost question: increasing subnet ranges is free but adding large CIDRs might conflict with our VPC plan. If we expand, we should document new IP ranges in infra inventory and update route tables.

ben: I'll draft the AWS quota request. Proposal:
- Increase ENIs per-instance to support p4/g5 max attachments
- Increase Elastic IPs/IPv4 addresses per region from 4096 -> 8192 for the account
- Request VPC secondary CIDR /19 for gpu-subnets in us-west-1
- Ask for EC2 quota for `Network Interfaces` by AZ to +50%

alex: Please include the affected clusters: eks-prod-gpu-usw1 (cluster-id: clu-02g5), eks-staging-gpu-usw1 (clu-02g5-stg). Also note impact: job failures, node join flaps, autoscaler thrash.

maya: Quick workaround while AWS processes: 1) spin up a small GKE/GCP gpu pool in us-west1-b (if policy allows) or 2) create a dedicated EKS cluster in a separate AWS account/project where quotas are free. Both have onboarding time.

ben: Opening support case now. Creating internal ticket INFRA-3421 and AWS case #1234567890. I'll paste links once created.

ops-bot: Created internal ticket INFRA-3421: https://tickets.redwood.local/INFRA-3421 and AWS support case 1234567890. Status: pending.

judy: Also flagging this with SRE oncall for possible reschedule of big jobs: @sre-oncall please hold new 64-GPU runs until we confirm quota increase or temporary mitigation.

alex: Thanks — will pause job queue. Keep me posted on case updates. :thumbsup:

ben: AWS case updated: support requested ENI quota increase and VPC secondary CIDR. ETA from AWS: 48-72 hours. I'll follow up if they ask for architecture details.

maya: If AWS asks, include our projected scaling curve: +200 GPUs in us-west1 over next 30 days, 4x peak pod density per node using prefix delegation.

ops-bot: INFRA-3421 updated: AWS case 1234567890 - support reply requested more details about instance types. Assigned to ben.

judy: Closing note: consider evaluating Amazon VPC Lattice or Calico IPAM later for long-term density improvements. For now, network quota increase is primary.

alex: Ack, thanks everyone.
